title: Islamic calendar wheel
subject: Arabic
unit: Summer 1: Dates and days of the week; my electronic games
source: Written for arabic/y5 lesson 15 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Islamic calendar wheel)
intro: Lesson 15: Months and dates: the Islamic calendar. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Write the number of each month (١ to ١٢) in its segment. Colour Ramadan and Dhul-Hijjah.

panels.title: The moon decides
points: Each month starts with the هِلَال
The Hijri year began with the Hijrah

panels.title: Saying a date
points: عِيدُ الأَضْحَى فِي شَهْرِ ذِي الحِجَّةِ

questions.q: In which month is Eid al-Adha?

Islamic calendar wheel on the pupil PDF: write the twelve months in order (copying the harakat) and mark three special times: رَمَضَان، ذُو الحِجَّة، مُحَرَّم (the new year). Then write one sentence: ... فِي شَهْرِ ...
questions.a: Twelve months in order and one correct sentence, for example: نَصُومُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ

questions.q: Extend: which month is it now in the Islamic calendar? (Ask at home or check the masjid timetable.)
Stretch: why is the Hijri year about eleven days shorter?
questions.a: It follows the moon: 12 months of 29 or 30 days
A) شَوَّال. رَمَضَان is 9th, شَوَّال is 10th.

questions.q: Think again: why does Ramadan move earlier each year?
questions.a: The Islamic year follows the moon and is shorter
